identity.title: Counter-rotation and High-velocity Outflow in the Parsec-scale Molecular Torus of NGC 1068

paper_type_evidence.quote: we obtained new ALMA observations of HCN ($J=3\to 2$) at 1.4 pc (20 mas) resolution.

evidence.quote: We adopt the Ringberg Standards for NGC 1068 (cite: 1997Ap&SS.248....9B), which assigns the scale 1$''$ = 70 pc.

question.value: What are the geometry and kinematics of the parsec-scale molecular torus of NGC 1068, as traced by HCN (3-2) at 1.4 pc resolution?

evidence.quote: In an effort to untangle the complicated geometry and kinematics of the molecular torus of NGC 1068, we obtained new ALMA observations of HCN ($J=3\to 2$) at 1.4 pc (20 mas) resolution.
We used ALMA to observe NGC 1068 in Band 6 during ALMA Cycle 5 (project code 2017.1.01666.S).
We used ALMA to observe NGC 1068 in Band 6 during ALMA Cycle 5

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: three continuum windows of 1.875 GHz each plus one HCN(3-2) window; ~1.0 km/s channels, ~1000 km/s bandwidth

evidence.quote: The HCN line observation has channel-width $\sim$1.0 km s$^{-1}$ and spans $\sim$1000 km s$^{-1}$ total bandwidth.
We used the longest baseline configuration available for Band 6 during Cycle 5, C43-10
with baselines ranging from 41.4 m to 16.2 km
The common restoring beam is $19.9\times19.1$ mas, PA 79.8$^\circ$
The largest recoverable structure is about 0.32$''$, or 22 pc at the distance of NGC 1068.

sensitivity.value: 1.6 mJy/beam per ~10 km/s channel (median); continuum rms 6.2 uJy/beam

evidence.quote: the median line channel sensitivity is 1.6 mJy beam$^{-1}$.
the total integration time on source was 14.5 hours
The source was observed in nine execution blocks between 10 October 2017 and 24 October 2017.

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate, self-calibrate and image continuum and HCN cube

method.value: CASA pipeline calibration, 4 phase-only self-cal cycles on continuum applied to lines, Briggs imaging, uv continuum subtraction, ~10 km/s channels

evidence.quote: We performed four cycles of phase-only self-calibration on the continuum data (cite: 1989ASPC....6..185C), and the solutions were applied to the spectral line data.

method.value: Gauss-Hermite polynomial fit to each spectrum in the cube

evidence.quote: We measured the radial velocity field using Gauss-Hermite polynomial fits to each spectrum in the HCN data cube

A Gauss-Hermite polynomial was fitted to each extracted HCN spectrum, and Monte Carlo realizations of the spectrum were generated by adding a randomly generated noise spectrum scaled to the observed rms.

method.value: Extract spectrum at S1; subtract mean of spectra 1.4 pc NE and SW to correct for emission

evidence.quote: we averaged the spectra from positions 1.4 pc (one beam) northeast and southwest of the nucleus and subtracted the result from the nuclear spectrum.

validation.value: Blue wing present in both raw and corrected spectra

evidence.quote: The blue wing appears on both the raw and corrected spectra, and so it is likely not an artifact of the emission correction.

method.value: Spectra at each pixel (0.2 pc) along major axis for r>=1.2 pc; two spectra along maser PA 131 deg for r<1.2 pc; Gauss-Hermite fit with Monte Carlo noise realizations

evidence.quote: Monte Carlo realizations of the spectrum were generated by adding a randomly generated noise spectrum scaled to the observed rms.
The average and standard deviation of $10^4$ trials respectively provide an estimate of the tangential velocity and its uncertainty.

assumptions.value: Intrinsic dispersion up to 90 km/s gives corrections smaller than uncertainties

evidence.quote: intrinsic velocity dispersions as high as $\sigma_r = 90$ km s$^{-1}$, comparable to the inferred rotation speeds, introduce corrections smaller than the measurement uncertainties.

validation.value: Compared with Keplerian curve from H2O masers

evidence.quote: The $r > 1.2$ pc rotation curve is consistent with an extrapolation of the Keplerian rotation curve.
imaged using CASA 5.1.1
there is a pronounced blue wing on the absorption profile that extends to roughly $-450$ km s$^{-1}$ relative to systemic
The inferred rotation speeds of the inner HCN disk reach $380\pm 30$ km s$^{-1}$

results_numeric.quantity: Largest deviation from Keplerian (3.4 pc NW)

evidence.quote: the measured rotational speed deviates from the predicted Keplerian rotation curve by $70\pm 40$ km s$^{-1}$
The median uncertainty is 30 km s$^{-1}$.
The orientation of the HCN major axis is PA $\sim 114\ensuremath{^\circ}$
Keplerian rotation around a central mass of $1.66\times 10^7\,\mbox{M}_\odot$

findings_qualitative.value: Outer disk (1.2-7 pc) counter-rotates relative to the inner disk, with rotation consistent with Keplerian about same central mass

evidence.quote: The outer disk, which extends to $\sim 7$ pc radius, counter-rotates relative to the inner disk.

findings_qualitative.value: HCN velocity field is complex along the CO outflow axis

evidence.quote: the HCN radial velocity field is more complex along the molecular outflow axis

claims.hypothesis: Is there a high-velocity molecular outflow in the nuclear region?
claims.experiment: Extract the HCN absorption spectrum toward S1, correct for emission
claims.result: Blue wing extends to about -450 km/s
claims.finding: Outflow speeds approach 450 km/s, exceeding CO(6-5) maxima of 400 km/s

evidence.quote: The excess blueshifted absorption is consistent with outflow velocities approaching 450 km s$^{-1}$

claims.hypothesis: Does the torus consist of kinematically distinct disks?
claims.experiment: Tangential velocity rotation curve along the major axis
claims.result: Inside 1.2 pc rotation follows the masers; 1.2-7 pc runs opposite
claims.finding: Counter-rotating, misaligned inner and outer disks

evidence.quote: between $r = 1.2$ pc and $r \sim 7$ pc, the outer HCN rotation curve runs counter to the inner maser disk rotation

claims.hypothesis: Origin of the outer counter-rotating disk
claims.experiment: Argument from angular momentum and literature
claims.finding: Outer disk likely formed from recently introduced gas (infall or captured dwarf); speculative

evidence.quote: It seems likely that the counter-rotating outer disk formed from gas that has been more recently introduced

limitations_admitted.value: Method does not correct for unknown intrinsic velocity dispersion; outflow and disk emission blended in the beam along the minor axis

evidence.quote: Note that this method does not correct for the unknown, intrinsic velocity dispersion of the gas.

referee_caveats_inferred: Blue absorption wing could partly reflect beam-blended emission or continuum structure
Rotation curve uncertainties are large; Keplerian consistency is weakly constrained
